title: How to Spot Fake Moncler & Canada Goose on Vinted (and What to Do If You're Sent One)
intro: Moncler and Canada Goose are two of the most counterfeited winter-coat brands in the world, and Vinted's low prices attract both genuine sellers and replica sellers. This guide covers exactly how to check a coat before you buy — badge, neck tag, hologram and QR code — and what to do if you're sent a fake.

body.heading: Why these two brands are the fake-flag
paragraphs: Moncler and Canada Goose are faked more than almost any other clothing brand, because a genuine jacket sells for hundreds of pounds while a replica can be bought for a fraction and resold at a huge profit. That makes them prime bait on Vinted, where sellers know buyers are hunting for a bargain.

The good news is that both brands have specific, well-documented authentication tells that haven't changed much — the badge, the neck tag, and the hologram or QR code. Learn these and you can filter out most fakes from listing photos before you ever part with money.

The better news: Vinted's Buyer Protection covers you if a coat arrives and turns out to be fake, as long as you report it within 48 hours of delivery. So the risk is a delay and a refund, not necessarily a loss — provided you know what to check and act fast.

body.heading: Moncler: the four things to check
paragraphs: 1. **The neck tag.** On a genuine Moncler, the "MONCLER" lettering is crisp and evenly stitched with white thread. Fakes almost always have thinner, weaker lettering and are surrounded by black stitching instead of white. This is the single most reliable tell.

2. **The arm badge.** Counterfeit badges pack in too much stitching, making the "MONCLER" text look thick and heavy — the opposite of the neck-tag problem. The "M" and "R" on a fake badge are usually the most obviously over-thick characters.

3. **The QR code / authenticity tag.** Modern Moncler uses a hologram QR-code tag sewn under the care labels. On a genuine coat the Moncler logo on this tag has a white or silver outline; on fakes it has a black outline. The code itself can be checked on Moncler's official site (code.moncler.com).
4. **The zipper.** Fake zippers often look scratched or worn, with the Moncler logo paint flaking off, even on a supposedly new coat.

If you can only check one thing from photos, check the neck tag stitching colour and lettering weight — it catches the majority of fakes. For more on this, [see our guide to spotting fakes generally](/guides/vinted-scams-buyer-protection).

body.heading: Canada Goose: badge, hologram and fur
paragraphs: 1. **The badge.** On a genuine Canada Goose, the letters and maple leaves are thin and precise. Fakes have thicker, boxier lettering and chunkier leaves — and on the worst fakes, letters are visibly connected or out of place. This is the first thing to look at.

2. **The hologram tag.** Canada Goose's official position is that the hologram on the tag is the authenticity marker. On a genuine jacket the hologram is subtly reflective; on a fake it's excessively shiny and the colours are over-saturated. If a tag has a QR code on it, treat it as a red flag.

3. **The fur (older models only).** Canada Goose used genuine coyote fur until 2021, when the brand stopped using fur entirely. So a supposedly-new jacket with real fur is a contradiction — and even on older jackets, fake fur is thinner and less dense than the real thing.
4. **The neck tag and content label.** On fakes, the "CANADA GOOSE" lettering is thicker and harder to read, and the "®" symbol is often jammed up against the word instead of separated.
The badge and the hologram are the two checks that catch the vast majority of fakes, and both are visible in most listing photos if you ask the seller for a close-up.

body.heading: How to check before you buy on Vinted
paragraphs: First, request specific photos. A genuine seller of a £400 coat will happily send close-ups of the badge, the neck tag and the hologram; a fake seller will be vague or reuse listing photos. If they refuse close-ups or the photos are blurry on exactly the areas above, walk away.

Second, check the price against reality. Both brands hold their value — a Moncler or Canada Goose at a fraction of the going rate is either fake or a scam. Use a sold-price tool to see what genuine coats actually sell for, so you know what a realistic price looks like. See [how to see sold prices on Vinted](/guides/how-to-see-sold-prices-on-vinted).

Third, stay inside Vinted's payment system. Never complete the sale by bank transfer or outside the app — off-platform payment has no protection, and it's the classic move when someone is selling a fake. Read [our full Vinted scams guide](/guides/vinted-scams-buyer-protection) for the pattern.

Finally, act fast on arrival. You have 48 hours from delivery to report a problem, so inspect the badge, tag and hologram the day the coat arrives, not a week later. See [how to handle delivery problems](/guides/vinted-delivery-issues-troubleshooting).

body.heading: What to do if you're sent a fake
paragraphs: 1. Don't panic and don't contact the seller for an off-app refund — that's how scammers get you to give up your protection. Stay in the app.
2. Raise a "not as described" issue through the order screen within 48 hours of delivery, with clear photos of the tells you found (badge, tag, hologram) as evidence.
3. Vinted's Buyer Protection will review it and, if it agrees the item is counterfeit, refund you — usually after you return the coat.
4. If Vinted's automated ruling goes against you, escalate and ask for a human review, flagging the specific authentication points. Keep every message in the app.
This is exactly the same recovery path as any other scam on Vinted, covered step-by-step in [what to do about scams and buyer protection](/guides/vinted-scams-buyer-protection).

body.heading: How an alert helps you buy the real thing
paragraphs: The frustrating reality of these brands is that genuine coats at fair prices sell within minutes — the replicas are the ones that linger. If you're checking manually, by the time you've done your authentication checks someone else has already bought the genuine one.

A saved-search alert flips this: the moment a Moncler or Canada Goose in your size and price range is listed, you're notified and can move fast — request the badge/tag photos, run the checks above, and buy before it goes. That's the practical way to combine speed with safety.

faq.question: How can I tell if a Moncler jacket on Vinted is real?
faq.answer: Check the neck tag first — genuine Moncler has crisp white stitching and evenly weighted lettering, while fakes have thinner text with black stitching. Then check the arm badge (fakes are over-thick), the hologram QR tag (genuine has a white/silver logo outline, fake has black), and the zipper. Ask for close-up photos before buying.

faq.question: How can I tell if a Canada Goose jacket is fake?
faq.answer: Check the badge — genuine lettering and maple leaves are thin and precise, fakes are thick and boxy with connected letters. Check the hologram tag (genuine is subtly reflective, fakes are over-shiny), and remember Canada Goose stopped using fur in 2021, so a 'new' jacket with real fur is a red flag.

faq.question: What do I do if I bought a fake Moncler or Canada Goose on Vinted?
faq.answer: Raise a 'not as described' issue through the order screen within 48 hours of delivery, with photos of the badge, tag and hologram as evidence. Vinted's Buyer Protection will review it and refund you if it agrees the item is counterfeit — usually after you return it.

faq.question: Should I pay for a Moncler or Canada Goose outside Vinted?
faq.answer: Never. Off-platform payment has no buyer protection, and it's the classic move when someone is selling a fake. Keep every transaction inside Vinted's payment system so Buyer Protection applies.

faq.question: Do Moncler and Canada Goose hold their value on Vinted?
faq.answer: Yes, both are among the brands that hold value best — which is exactly why they're counterfeited. A genuine coat at a price far below the going rate is usually fake or a scam, so check the sold-price reality before you buy.
